title: Financial Product Trading Policy

tiers.name: all directors and employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of Ryman and its subsidiaries (Ryman Group), who must follow this policy when trading Ryman's quoted financial products. Subject to the fundamental insider trading rule, the trading windows and the short-term trading rule, but no preclearance system unless also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors, the group chief executive, all senior executive team (SET) members and their direct reports, all Ryman finance team members, all Ryman legal team members, and anyone else notified or designated by the Chief Financial Officer. Must obtain prior written consent before trading at any time, and provide post-trade notice to the CFO.

tiers.name: family, and trusts and companies controlled
tiers.description: Family of Restricted Persons, and trusts and companies controlled by them; the Restricted Person is responsible for their actions.

windows.start_anchor: day on which Ryman's full-year results are released
day on which Ryman's half-year results are released

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Chair of the Audit, Finance and Risk Committee may specify additional blackout periods from time to time. Trading outside the trading windows, or during such additional periods, is 'trading in blackout' and is a breach of the policy for everyone the policy applies to, not only Restricted Persons; the policy does not state whether ad hoc periods are confidential.

rules.section: What financial products are covered by this policy?
rules.detail: Ryman products expressly includes derivatives of any quoted financial product of the Ryman Group, with no venue limitation. Ordinary directors/employees may deal in such derivatives only within the trading windows, subject to the fundamental insider trading rule, but face no preclearance requirement.
rules.evidence: any other quoted financial products of the Ryman Group from time to time, and derivatives of any quoted financial products of the Ryman Group

rules.section: What financial products are covered by this policy?; Appendix
rules.detail: A derivative over Ryman products is itself a Ryman product, so a Restricted Person must obtain prior written consent from the relevant approver before dealing in it, at any time (not only within trading windows).
rules.evidence: Before trading in Ryman products, at any time, Restricted Persons must, in writing: notify the appropriate person set out below of their intention to trade in financial products, and seek consent to do so

rules.detail: Hedging is not named anywhere in the policy.

rules.section: What is meant by 'trade' and what is excluded?
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is caught because 'trade' includes agreeing to buy or sell; for ordinary employees this is only subject to trading windows and the insider trading rule.
rules.evidence: trade includes buying or selling Ryman products (or agreeing to do so), whether as principal or agent

rules.detail: An agreement to sell (such as a prepaid forward) by a Restricted Person is a trade requiring prior written consent at any time.
rules.evidence: Before trading in Ryman products, at any time, Restricted Persons must, in writing ... seek consent to do so

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.

rules.section: What financial products are covered by this policy?
rules.detail: CFDs are not named but fall within 'derivatives of any quoted financial products of the Ryman Group'; ordinary employees face only the trading window and insider trading constraints.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any quoted financial products of the Ryman Group

rules.detail: A CFD over Ryman products is a Ryman product and thus requires prior written consent for a Restricted Person.
rules.evidence: Before trading in Ryman products, at any time, Restricted Persons must, in writing ... seek consent to do so

rules.detail: Margin lending is not addressed anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Ryman products is not addressed and is not swept into the 'trade' definition, which covers only buying, selling and agreeing to do so.
Secured financing arrangements are not addressed anywhere in the policy.

Applies to everyone the policy covers, not only Restricted Persons: refrain from buying and selling Ryman shares within a three-month period unless exceptional circumstances are discussed with, and prior approval to trade obtained from, the Group Chief Financial Officer.
rules.evidence: Refrain from engaging in short-term trading of Ryman shares (defined as buying or selling within a three-month period) unless exceptional circumstances apply. Where exceptional circumstances apply, you must discuss these circumstances with the Group Chief Financial Officer and obtain prior approval to trade.

clearance.approver: Chief Financial Officer (most Restricted Persons); the CFO seeks consent from the CEO; the CEO and any director other than the Chair seek consent from the Board Chair; the Board Chair seeks consent from the Chair of the Audit, Finance and Risk Committee
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly following completion of the trade
clearance.section: Appendix: Additional Trading Restrictions for Restricted Persons
clearance.evidence: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after it is granted. A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading.

short_term.basis: buying or selling within the period
carve_outs: exceptional circumstances discussed with and approved in advance by the Group Chief Financial Officer
short_term.evidence: Refrain from engaging in short-term trading of Ryman shares (defined as buying or selling within a three-month period) unless exceptional circumstances apply.

exceptions.evidence: acquisitions/disposals of Ryman products by gift or inheritance
the subscription for, or the issue of, new Ryman products such as an issue of new shares under a rights issue or a dividend reinvestment plan (if this becomes relevant)
Nothing in this policy precludes a Restricted Person in possession of material information from acquiring Ryman products under a short-term incentive or long-term incentive
or acquiring or disposing of KiwiSaver products which may hold Ryman products as part of their portfolio

exceptions.approver: Chief Financial Officer, Chief Executive, Board Chair or Chair of the Audit, Finance and Risk Committee, per the consent hierarchy
exceptions.evidence: Restricted Persons are not permitted to trade any Ryman products during any other period unless a specific exemption is obtained from the appropriate person listed above.

exemption_authority: Chair of the Audit, Finance and Risk Committee may declare additional blackout periods. A specific exemption to trade outside the open windows or during an additional blackout period may be granted in exceptional circumstances by the appropriate approver in the consent hierarchy (CFO, CEO, Board Chair or Audit, Finance and Risk Committee Chair).
jurisdiction_overlays: NZX Main Board and NZX debt market (NZDX)
New Zealand Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (Part 5 insider trading; relevant interest disclosure by directors and senior managers)

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other quoted financial products of the Ryman Group from time to time, and derivatives of any quoted financial products of the Ryman Group
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No venue restriction is placed on the derivative itself, only on the underlying (which must be quoted), so an OTC put/call collar written by a bank over RYM shares is a Ryman product and a 'trade' under this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: It is prohibited for anyone to which this policy applies to trade in any Ryman products except in the following periods ... Trading outside of the trading windows ... is known as trading in blackout and is a breach of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many ASX policies where only Restricted Persons face closed periods, RYM's window restriction applies to all directors and employees, so collar entry, unwind, roll or settlement by anyone must fall inside an open trading window absent a specific exemption.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Restricted Person must comply with any disclosure obligations it has under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (including disclosure of relevant interests in quoted financial products by directors and senior managers of listed issuers)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar and a pledge of shares as loan security would likely require separate relevant-interest disclosure under the FMCA, on top of this policy's consent process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy does not address margin lending, pledging, or any other secured financing arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares faces no express policy bar, but because 'trade' is broad and the policy is silent on encumbrance, it is unclear whether granting security itself is treated as a dealing requiring consent or window compliance.

summary: A funded collar is workable for RYM shares, subject to timing and (for some directors and executives) a consent process. Because Ryman products expressly includes derivatives of quoted financial products with no stated venue limit, an OTC put and call fall within scope, but ordinary directors and employees who are not Restricted Persons face no preclearance requirement at all, only the requirement to trade inside the two open trading windows (full-year results release to 31 August; half-year results release to 31 January) and the fundamental insider trading prohibition. Restricted Persons (directors, the group CE, SET and their direct reports, and finance/legal team members) must obtain prior written consent from an escalating hierarchy (CFO, then CEO, then Board Chair, then Audit Committee Chair), valid for only 10 trading days, and cannot trade outside the open windows without a specific exemption. The policy is entirely silent on hedging, margin lending, pledging and secured financing, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares faces no express prohibition, though its treatment as a 'dealing' is untested by the text. Both a general and Restricted Person collar counterparty would need to time entry, unwind and settlement to fall within an open trading window and, if a Restricted Person, obtain fresh consent for each step.
